items.title: docs(id): land the validated-reply contract in world_net module docs (#6670)
items.body: Phase 4 of #6669 (closing inventory, #6670): lands the validated-reply contract statement in the `world_net.rs` module documentation, in its final as-built form. Comment-only change — 27 lines of module docs, no behavior change: 1. A field that constitutes the answer is required and typed; missing/mistyped is a malformed-reply error naming the field. Success fields are never defaulted. 2. Optional means absent-or-null, never mistyped (the `parse_module_info_reply` shape). 3. Typed payloads are decoded at extraction, not cloned — validate-then-return. 4. A list reply's entries are part of the answer; a listing is complete or it errors. 5. Extraction lives in `WorldClient`, never in callers. The full per-method inventory with file:line evidence, and required dispositions (a)–(g), are posted on #6670. The two lax extractions the inventory found were filed as follow-ups per #6670's acceptance rule, not patched here: #6777 (`set_execution_profile` whole-frame return, disposition (a)) and #6778 (`record_pages` mistyped `next_after`, disposition (d)). --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Documentation** * Clarified how replies are extracted, including required and optional answer fields, payload validation, and handling of malformed list entries.

items.title: fix(id): validate update.requested in set_execution_profile replies (#6777)
items.body: Fixes #6777. ## Problem `WorldClient::set_execution_profile` checked only `reply["type"] != "execution_profile"` and returned the whole frame — a reply with no `update` at all counted as a successful profile change for both consumers (the operator-facing pretty-print in `commands/world.rs`, and manifest apply's `SetProfile` step). This is the setter leg of #6635: the getter already extracts `update.requested` with a "host returned a malformed execution profile" refusal; the setter never did (found by the #6670 Phase 4 closing inventory, disposition (a)). ## Fix Following the file's validated-reply pattern (`parse_caps_ceiling_reply`, #6636): - New `WorldClient::parse_set_execution_profile_reply`: non-`execution_profile` frames bail with the host's message (unchanged refusal behavior); otherwise `update.requested` must be present **and** decode as `crate::world_limits::WorldExecutionProfile`, else bail "host returned a malformed execution profile" — the getter's exact error, so setter and getter agree on what a valid frame is. - On success the frame is returned **unchanged** (byte-identical), so both consumers keep their current shapes; no caller changes. - `set_execution_profile` now routes its reply through the parser. ## Verification (laptop) - New test `set_execution_profile_reply_requires_a_valid_requested`: well-formed frame returned unchanged; missing update / missing / null / mistyped `requested` all refused with the malformed-profile error; error frames still bail with the host's message. **Passes.** - `cargo test --lib world_net`: **45 passed** (all sibling reply parsers and client tests green). - The changed hunks are rustfmt-clean (the crate has pre-existing fmt drift elsewhere on main under this toolchain; untouched). --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: fix(id): refuse a mistyped module_hash in the admin history begin frame (#6641)
items.body: ## What `WorldClient::admin_event_history` read the `event_history_begin` frame's `module_hash` with `.as_str().map(...)` — every non-string value (number, bool, array, object) collapsed to `None`, the legitimate "world has no module" value, so a malformed export header silently recorded a world with a module as module-less (and `world_fixture::record` then baked that false provenance into the fixture header). Every sibling field in the same frame is strict; only this one was lenient. Issue #6642 is a duplicate of #6641 (same function, field, and evidence) and has been closed as a duplicate; this PR is the single fix for both. ## Change - Factor the begin-frame head parsing into `WorldClient::parse_event_history_begin` and give `module_hash` the same match-and-bail treatment `info_details` got for #6633: absent / `null` → `None`, string → `Some(hash)`, anything else → `Err` ("history reply has a malformed module_hash: expected string or null, got …"). No behavior change for conforming hosts (`ServerFrame::EventHistoryBegin` serializes the hash as string-or-null by construction). - Regression test `admin_event_history_begin_requires_a_string_or_null_module_hash`: string / null / missing controls plus number / bool / array / object refusals, with sibling fields verified intact. ## Verification (laptop, this branch) - `cargo test -p id --lib admin_event_history -- --test-threads=1`: new test passes. - `cargo test -p id --lib world_fixture -- --test-threads=1`: 28 passed, 0 failed (the fixture record/replay consumers). Closes #6641. Filed by the repo queue worker, lane code-a, in fallback mode (queue backend down 2026-11-06/07; issue #6641 claimed via a fallback claim marker on the issue). --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved validation of event history headers, including checks for world IDs, sequence numbers, completeness, and event counts. * Event history headers now accept a missing or null module hash, while rejecting module hashes in unsupported formats.
